description:
Thread title: [0.98a] Slay the Sector v0.5.2 (beta)

A Slay the Spire style roguelite, played inside your Starsector campaign.

Every Act is a branching map of beacons: pick your path to the Boss.

Download v0.5.2 (beta)
Source code on GitHub | All releases

Requires: Starsector 0.98a. No other mods needed.

Save compatibility

Can be added to an ongoing game: yes. The Descent Relay appears the next time you load.
Your campaign is safe: a Run changes nothing except a credit Payout at the end. XP, skills, story points, marines, reputation, bounties, cargo and salaries are all restored.
Can be removed: not yet. A save that has used the mod needs it to load. Finish your Run and keep a backup before uninstalling.
Other mods: compatible. Modded factions and ships show up as playable factions and as enemies. Tested with Nexerelin, Random Assortment of Things, Combat Chatter, MagicLib, LazyLib, LunaLib and GraphicsLib.

What is it?
The Descent Relay has opened somewhere in the core worlds. Dock with it, plug into its combat simulation, and fight your way down The Descent: three Acts of branching battles, shops, events and Bosses, with a fleet you build as you go. Your real fleet waits safely at the Relay. When the Run ends, win or lose, you get it back exactly as you left it, plus a credit Payout for how deep you went.

The Descent Relay calls you from the Intel screen: Show on map, Lay in course.

How a Run plays

Find the Relay: the Intel screen has it under Important, with Show on map and Lay in course.
Pick a faction and a fleet: any faction with enough ships, modded ones included. Spend 30 DP on its ships, or press Random.
Choose your path: every Act is a map of beacons. Pick the next one, fly there, and see what waits.
Grow your fleet: after each win, take a ship, an officer or weapons. Supplies are the only currency, so repairs, shops and fleet size all compete for them.
Beat the Boss: each Act ends with one. Win, choose a Boss reward, and descend deeper.

After each win, pick a ship, an officer or weapons. Watch the fleet's DP cap.

What you can meet in the Descent
Combat: a standard fight. Win for supplies and a Reward pick.
Elite: a stronger fleet surrounds you. Break out with most of your fleet.
Ambush: the enemy runs. Destroy its marked flagship before it escapes.
Events: a battle station (assault it or trade with it), sabotage, a side battle where you pick who to help, a convoy raid.
Shop: ships, weapons, officers, repairs, D-mod removal and a bigger fleet cap, all paid in supplies. Shops grow with each Act.
Rest: a free repair, an S-mod, an officer level, or removing a ship's D-mods.
Treasure: one rare prize.
Boss: the end of each Act. Its reward: an extra S-mod slot and an S-mod, a bigger fleet, or a Remnant warship.

Progression: Ascension and Records
Winning a Run unlocks harder levels for that faction, from Gamma to Omega (named after the AI cores of vanilla and Random Assortment of Things). Each level adds a handicap and a bigger Payout. Omega hides one last fight.
Your Records and three small starting bonuses are kept across all your saves.

Each Act ends with a Boss. No retreat.

This is a beta
Everything in the mod works, but it is still being polished:

Balance is not finished. Some fights may feel too hard or too easy, and some prices too cheap or too expensive. Your feedback is exactly what will fix that.
Bugs are possible, especially in the later Acts, which have had less play time.

Found a problem, or something felt off? Please tell me! The easiest way is the Report a problem page on GitHub: pick "Report a bug" or "Balance feedback", and a short form guides you (you only need a free GitHub account). Describe what happened in your own words. If you can, drag and drop the file starsector.log from your Starsector folder into the form: it helps a lot.
Replies in this thread are welcome too.

Most numbers (difficulty, rewards, prices, map shape) can also be changed in data/config/settings.json, if you like to tinker.

Changelog
0.5.2 (beta)
Fixed a crash when confirming the Starting pick with Combat Chatter installed.
Fixed a related error with Nexerelin's salvage scavenger dialog near the Run fleet.

0.5.1 (beta)
Balance
Act 2 and Act 3 no longer start easier than the end of the previous Act: fights climb from the previous Act's last fight.
Supply rewards grow with the Act (x1.0 / x1.5 / x2.0), since the fleet gets bigger and costs more to repair.
The true Boss and the battle station now start at full combat readiness.

Shops
One page of stock per Act (Act 2 = 2 pages, Act 3 = 3 pages).
Buy +10 Fleet DP cap for 100 supplies (first card of every Shop).

Interface
Ship cards: hover a ship's name to see its fit, press F1 for its weapons, fighters and hullmods.
The end of a Run posts an intel report with a notification: result, Payout, how deep you went, and what you unlocked.

Other
Debug commands for the Console Commands mod: sts status, sts unlock, sts act 2-4, sts supplies (handy to test Act 4).
The mod is now under the MIT license (LICENSE file included).
Bug reports and balance feedback: friendly forms on the GitHub Issues page.

0.5.0 (beta)
First public release: three Acts, eight kinds of beacons, Shops, Rests, Treasures, Events, Boss rewards, Ascension levels and cross-save Records.

Full history in the changelog.

Credits
Thanks to the people whose work and open source code taught me how Starsector mods are made, and whose mods I love playing:

wispborne, for the Starsector IntelliJ Template this project started from, and for everything they do for the modding community. I learned to make my first mod with their tutorials.
Lukas22041, for Second In Command and Random Assortment of Things, the inspiration for this mod and a great example of what a Starsector mod can be. I never play Starsector without Lukas's mods.
Histidine91, for Nexerelin, a reference for nearly every campaign question. Histidine showed me how deep modding can go, and I've spent many evenings reading Nexerelin's code to learn how the game loop works.
tracesfx, for the starsector-modding skill: the build, validation and log tools, and the API notes this project relies on.

And to Alex and the Fractal Softworks team for Starsector <3

Permissions: the mod is under the MIT license: use, change, fork or redistribute it freely, as long as the copyright notice and the license text stay with it.

AI use disclaimer
Some or all assets and code in this mod were created using AI tools:
Code: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), through Claude Code. It wrote most of the Java code, the build and test tooling configuration, and the design and API documentation.
Code review: Claude was also used to review each milestone for bugs before release. No line of code reaches a release without a human review.
Art: the banner at the top of this post was made with Z-Image Turbo (Alibaba's Tongyi Lab), an open image model run locally in ComfyUI, starting from vanilla Starsector portraits; its three captains are a nod to Slay the Spire's Ironclad, Silent and Defect. Nothing in the mod itself uses AI art: map and node icons are vanilla Starsector sprites.

How it was made: I designed the mod (the Run, the beacon types, the rules and the balance) and directed every change. Each milestone was then played and tested in game by me, against a checklist, before it was merged. The full source and the design notes are public on GitHub.

aiDescription: Introduces The Descent Relay, allowing players to enter combat simulations with a temporary fleet. Players navigate branching maps across three acts, engaging in battles, events, and shops while managing supplies. Winning runs unlocks harder difficulty levels and provides credit payouts without affecting the main campaign's progress.
